definitions.meaning: The double pump that pushes blood around both loops of the circulation.
A vessel that carries blood away from the heart, whatever oxygen that blood carries.
A vessel that carries blood back towards the heart.
The artery from the heart to the lungs; the exception that carries oxygen-poor blood.
Blood travelling in two loops, passing through the heart twice per circuit.
The loop between heart and lungs, where blood loads oxygen.
The loop between heart and body, where blood delivers oxygen.
Blood rich in oxygen, shown red, travelling from lungs or heart to the body.
Blood low in oxygen, shown blue, travelling back to the heart and on to the lungs.
Plant vessels that carry water and minerals upward from roots to leaves.
Plant tubes that move food made in the leaves to wherever it is needed.

mechanismSteps: The heart is a double pump - the left side pushes oxygen-rich blood to the body, the right side pushes oxygen-poor blood to the lungs.
Two loops: heart to lungs, heart to body - the pulmonary loop loads oxygen, the systemic loop delivers it, and blood passes through the heart twice.
Xylem lifts water; phloem shares food - xylem carries water and minerals up from the soil, phloem moves leaf-made food to where it is needed.
A common mistake: arteries always carry oxygen - the pulmonary artery carries oxygen-poor blood to the lungs, because arteries are named by direction away from the heart.
objectives: Describe the heart as a double pump and trace the pulmonary and systemic loops
State what xylem and phloem each carry in a plant
Correct the arteries-always-oxygen claim using the pulmonary artery and the direction rule
subject: science
title: Transport: blood and the double circulation

trap.explanation: The slip: Arteries are drawn in red and carry blood away from the heart, so they feel like the oxygen pipe. The fix: The pulmonary artery is the exception: it carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs. In class, replay the mistake scene: follow the pulmonary artery out of the right side of the heart - its blood is on its way to load oxygen, not deliver it.

workedExample: Test the colour rule on the pulmonary artery. Step 1 (s2): the pulmonary loop runs from the heart to the lungs, so the pulmonary artery carries blood away from the heart - an artery by direction. Step 2 (s4): that blood has just come back from the body, so it is oxygen-poor until the lungs reload it. The pulmonary artery is therefore an artery carrying deoxygenated blood, and the colour rule fails.
